2608.16353.title: HalluTracer: Hallucination Detection via Depth-Averaging Truth Signals
2608.16353.paper_summary: Even well-aligned large language models confidently generate factually incorrect text, making hallucination a persistent reliability risk in high-stakes deployments. These models nonetheless carry linearly separable truthfulness signals in their internal representations. Existing white-box detectors, however, collapse this evidence to isolated components or a single depth, discarding discriminative information distributed across the full forward pass. We introduce HalluTracer, a detection framework that reads and aggregates truthfulness evidence across every layer of the forward pass before the model emits any answer token. A geometric analysis reveals that the per-layer signals are weakly correlated, so that simple depth averaging suppresses layer-specific noise and captures nearly all linearly accessible information. Across six open-source language models and five hallucination benchmarks, HalluTracer consistently outperforms matched white-box baselines, with gains ranging from one to fourteen points. Collectively, our work recasts hallucination detection from a layer-selection problem into a depth-aggregation problem governed by the geometric sparsity of the truthfulness signal.
2608.16353.paper_summary_zh: 即使是對齊良好的大型語言模型也會自信地生成事實上不正確的文本，使得幻覺在高風險部署中成為持續的可靠性風險。儘管如此，這些模型在其內部表示中仍然攜帶線性可分的真實性信號。然而，現有的白盒檢測器卻將這些證據壓縮為孤立的組件或單一深度，丟棄了分佈在整個前向傳遞過程中的區分信息。我們引入了HalluTracer，一個檢測框架，該框架在模型發出任何答案標記之前，讀取並聚合每一層的真實性證據。幾何分析顯示，每層信號之間的相關性較弱，因此簡單的深度平均可以抑制特定層的噪音，並捕捉幾乎所有線性可訪問的信息。在六個開源語言模型和五個幻覺基準測試中，HalluTracer始終優於匹配的白盒基線，增益範圍從一到十四點。總體而言，我們的工作將幻覺檢測從層選擇問題重新構造為一個由真實性信號的幾何稀疏性所主導的深度聚合問題。
